19.24.name: 19.24.md
19.24.text:
copy-assignment operator: If the tok is a string or Sales_data object, the if statements that check if the two object have the same discriminant (have the same type of object held by the union) would take care of the guard against self-assignment. This is so because placement new expression will never be executed, and therefore, we would need not worry about an exception being thrown--the Token object is simply copied to itself.

move-assignment operator: If we move an object, however, we must include a guard against self-assignment. This can be done by enclosing the code in a check that would ignore the to moving an object to itself. (p. 536-537)

19.26.text:
```cpp
extern "C" int compute(int *, int);
extern "C" double compute(double *, double);
```

The declarations use a linkage directive, extern "C", to export a C++ function

(compute) to be used with C program. The declarations are illegal because the

compute is an overloaded function. The C language does not support function overloading.
